title: C1645 — Generator current sensor connector
introduction:
The generator, also called the alternator, supplies electrical power while the engine runs. I use this reference to connect the generator current sensor’s identity with its illustrated cavities, circuit descriptions and catalog entry. It is a seating chart for the connections, not a charging-system report card: knowing where a circuit belongs does not tell us how it is performing.

Read the identity table first, match the drawing’s cavity labels to the pin table, then consult the pigtail record. This page does not establish physical access, viewing side, test conditions or replacement methods. Box, Size and Used remain catalog fields without defined interpretations here, and the gauge convention is unspecified.

edits.why: I use the vertical cavity labels, rounded right-hand outline and stepped housing details on the left to navigate this particular drawing. Match labels directly to the Cavity column. The drawing’s layout does not establish a physical viewing side, release direction or mounting orientation.

Read each row across rather than treating the circuit names as a separate list. This keeps the cavity, circuit identifier, color, gauge, function and terminal identifier associated. The descriptions distinguish reference, return and sensor-related connections; they do not specify measured voltage, current or a charging-system verdict.

The catalog record connects the pigtail Number with its Service Part and Engineering Shell. I keep those identifiers separate so a housing designation is not mistaken for the service item. Material and gauge entries describe the listed record; they do not establish replacement-wire compatibility or installation instructions.
